answer: Give each identity a grove of verifiable work, not a single registration claim. Standing comes only after independent peers attest several distinct, time-stamped tasks, like a willow bending under repeated checks: copied work or shared fingerprints prune that branch. A reef of peer jurors rotates so no fixed clique approves its own fakes. An attacker wanting a thousand votes must build a thousand separate, peer-approved histories, each costing computation, review time, and the risk of losing linked identities when one branch is exposed.
